title: Google Project Zero cuts bug disclosures to 30 days amid AI threats
content_md: Google Project Zero will replace its “90+30” disclosure policy with shorter, fixed deadlines in response to AI-accelerated vulnerability discovery and exploitation. The transition is gradual and began on November 13, when the 30-day extension was removed from the vulnerability disclosure timeline. On February 2, 2027, the deadline will be further reduced to 60 days, and on January 3, 2028, it will shrink to just 30 days. Once the deadline expires, Project Zero will publish vulnerability details even if a fix is not available. Project Zero is Google’s vulnerability research team, focused on the discovery of serious security flaws in widely used software and hardware. Some of its notable recent findings include a .NET Framework zero-day , flaws in Chrome’s JavaScript engine and graphics components, and a Qualcomm chipset zero-day linked to NoviSpy spyware attacks . When the team finds a flaw, it reports it privately to the vendor and typically publishes the technical details after a set period, giving time for developing security updates and patches, as well as a margin for most users to apply them. Project Zero says AI has accelerated vulnerability discovery and exploitation, and made it easier for attackers to reverse-engineer fixes as soon as patches ship and develop working exploits.
